summary: Redwood AE/SE walked NovaApps through a migration demo focused on API parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered request/response mapping, streaming & tool-calling parity, embedding differences, cost/latency tradeoffs, Redwood Console observability, and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Customer agreed to provide prompts/traffic and to run a short hosted trial; Redwood will deliver parity spreadsheet and trial setup.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-29 16:00 UTC | Duration ~45m | Attendees listed above

00:00 Alex Gomez: thanks everyone for joining, yeah i think we have about 45 minutes today, quick agenda — demo of the API parity mapping, short console walkthrough, then q&a and next steps. Priya is our solutions engineer who will do the deep-dive.
00:20 John Park: great thanks Alex, quick context, we currently run a mix of OpenAI for chat generation, Anthropic for toxic content filtering, and Together for a few custom models. main concerns are latency (customer-facing chat), cost, and security (we're regulated).
00:40 Priya Shah: understood — we'll focus on request/response parity, streaming, embeddings differences, and how Redwood handles routing/caching to hit your latency SLOs.
01:05 Lisa Chen: do you have a one-to-one mapping for the OpenAI endpoint we use? our product uses the ChatCompletion API heavily, plus function calling for retrieval augmentation.
01:25 Priya Shah: yes, Alex i can share the parity sheet — essentially we map the chat endpoint to /v1/chat/completions equivalent, with a few param renames. streaming is supported and function/tool calling works similarly; we also have structured output helpers.
01:50 Alex Gomez: high level note — customers often forget KV cache/prefix caching impact. Redwood does automatic KV caching for repeated prefixes which helps latency for chat sessions.
02:10 Carlos Rivera: on embeddings, we use both OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and Together embeddings. how do vector dims and semantics match?
02:30 Priya Shah: embeddings vary but we provide recommended model mappings. usually semantic alignment needs a small anchor eval; we surface cosine similarity baseline comparisons in the parity doc. dims differ, but we also provide up/down projection options and reindexing guidance in the Console.
03:00 Sofia Diaz: security question — does Redwood support KMS and dedicated network (VPC) for private deployments?
03:20 Alex Gomez: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering or on-prem options; we'll include the SOC2 and network docs in the follow-up packet.
03:45 Priya Shah: demo time — i'll share my screen, starting with a simple mapping example: an OpenAI ChatCompletion request on the left, Redwood API call on the right.
04:10 [screen share sound-muted]
04:15 Priya Shah: here's a typical request, role/user/assistant arrays are identical, param rename: max_tokens -> max_tokens (same), temperature -> temp, top_p -> top_p. For function calling we accept the same json schema, we return a function_call block and you can pass it back the same way.
05:00 Lisa Chen: do you preserve the idempotency semantics? we rely on unique request ids for dedupe.
05:15 Priya Shah: Redwood supports idempotency keys per request header and we log them in traces.
05:35 Alex Gomez: on cost side, one-time mapping pitfalls are tokenization differences; we saw ~3-6% diff when customers moved from OpenAI to quantized variants depending on tokenizer. we'll put sample tokenization diffs in sheet.
06:00 John Park: how about streaming? we need sub-200ms first-byte latency for chat.
06:20 Priya Shah: streaming first-byte depends on model and hardware. Redwood's serving runtime pins small-batch fast paths and we can route to low-latency nodes for high-tier traffic — in benchmarks we hit ~120-180ms first byte for our small chat models. We'll propose a Dedicated pool if you need strict SLOs.
07:00 Carlos Rivera: Together models pack different kv cache behavior, does Redwood handle kv cache transfer for warm sessions?
07:18 Priya Shah: yes, KV cache is managed per session and we support serialization between compatible model variants; if switching families we'd recommend a brief warmup phase and Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/warmup parameters.
08:00 Alex Gomez: quick Console walkthrough — show per-route latency, token costs, token-level breakdowns and traces.
08:25 [console screenshare]
08:30 Priya Shah: here's a per-route panel, you can see token cost, avg latency, p50/p95, and a trace explorer that ties a single request across services. Useful for debugging function calls and model fallbacks.
09:15 Lisa Chen: can we hook our internal tracing (Jaeger)?
09:25 Priya Shah: yes you can forward traces or use our tracing hooks; we provide trace export and an api to correlate.
10:00 John Park: about model rollouts: we have a canary workflow currently. can Redwood do traffic splits and automatic fallback to OpenAI if something goes wrong?
10:18 Alex Gomez: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. For Hosted customers we can configure fallback to a different model or to an external endpoint — e.g., if a request goes over latency threshold or model fails, route to OpenAI as a backup.
10:55 Carlos Rivera: embedding reindexing — will we need to re-embed everything? that's expensive.
11:12 Priya Shah: often you can avoid full reindex by using a hybrid approach: run new embeddings on new items and dual-query both indices for a short window. We include recommended timelines in the parity sheet.
12:00 Sofia Diaz: compliance — audit logs, retention policy controls?
12:20 Alex Gomez: we expose audit logs, per-tenant retention controls, and you can set SSO/SAML + RBAC via the Console. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs and support a security workshop.
12:55 John Park: what about latency/cost optimization using Redwood Optimize?
13:10 Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize analyzes your traffic and suggests batching, quantization, and routing policy changes. For example, for lower-priority offline completions we suggested int8 quantized variants — estimates show 2-3x cost reduction with a modest latency increase. We can run an eval on your prompt set.
13:50 Alex Gomez: i'll highlight one real customer who reduced token spend by 35% via caching + model routing.
14:10 Lisa Chen: does Redwood provide a migration SDK or helper scripts?
14:22 Priya Shah: yes, we have starter SDKs with request/response mappers and a migration toolkit that converts common OpenAI params and function calls to Redwood equivalents. We'll include links.
14:45 John Park: demo of a live migration sample?
15:00 Priya Shah: sure — i'll run a quick live example: send a sample chat through OpenAI emulator then Redwood — showing streaming and function result.
15:30 [live demo run, slight audio overlap]
16:10 Priya Shah: you can see here the function call payload is identical; Redwood adds a trace id and logs the idempotency header.
16:45 Carlos Rivera: results look similar but we need to run an evaluation for hallucination/regression.
17:00 Priya Shah: absolutely — we'll run an eval suite across your prompt set. we can tie regressions to alerts in Console.
17:20 Sofia Diaz: final security nit — can keys be scoped per-route and rotated automatically?
17:35 Alex Gomez: yes, fine-grained API keys and automatic rotation via KMS integrations are supported on Private; for Hosted we support scoped keys and rotation APIs.
18:00 John Park: timeline question — assume we want to pilot in prod for a week, what's typical path?
18:15 Alex Gomez: typical: 1) parity mapping and small smoke test (1 week), 2) hosted 2-week trial or Dedicated pilot depending on SLOs (2 weeks), 3) expand to production with canary rollout (2-4 weeks). We'll put recommended dates in next steps.
18:40 Lisa Chen: cost estimate sensitivity — can you provide per-token cost comparisons?
18:55 Alex Gomez: yes we'll include a cost model spreadsheet that maps your traffic to Hosted and Dedicated options and shows projected unit economics with/without quantization.
19:20 [brief offline sidebar — attendees typing/chat]
21:00 Alex Gomez: ok quick recap and next steps: Alex to share parity spreadsheet + pricing; Priya to provision trial org and run baseline benchmarks; NovaApps to send representative prompt set & security contacts. schedule follow-up POC scoping in two weeks.
21:35 John Park: sounds good, thanks all. appreciate the focus on token deltas and KV cache.
21:50 Alex Gomez: thanks everyone, we'll email the packet and proposed times.
22:00 call ended with screen share off and follow-up calendar invites planned.
